segments.text: Think back to 25 years ago if you made a spreadsheet in Excel
You saved it directly to your computer's hard drive if that drive crashed before you back it up your work was gone
Today with something like Google sheets. You can close your laptop open your phone and pick up right where you left off
So where is that file while your devices are turned off?
Google keeps a copy on its own servers
When people talk about the cloud they are really just talking about computers you access over the internet the cloud serves two main purposes
First it acts as a remote storage locker for your files
But second it can actually run software programs over that internet connection
For modern technology keeping a copy of your spreadsheet is a solved problem
Storing a file takes very little computing effort
But watch what happens when you take that same spreadsheet share it with chat GPT and ask
Why did my expenses jump in March?
The AI does not have a pre-written answer sitting in a database. It has to generate its response from scratch
Calculating the most likely next word one at a time using math
Performing all that math requires an entirely different level of power
The energy it takes to actively write an AI response
Dorfs the energy it takes to passively save a file when an answer instantly pops up on your screen
It looks effortless
But underneath that clean interface is a massive grinding mathematical engine working behind the scenes
To understand the size of that engine we have to look at how AI processes text
Language models break text down into pieces called tokens
Each token is represented by a vector a dense grade of thousands of numbers that captures its initial meaning
As a token passes through the model's layers
The system uses attention and transformation to constantly update those thousands of numbers
Adjusting for the context of the words around it
Looking at this chart we see how fast the math adds up one token takes roughly a hundred billion calculations
Moving to the middle a short AI answer roughly 75 words takes about 10 trillion calculations
On the far right a
750 word conversation requires a staggering 100 trillion calculations
What feels like instant digital thought is actually trillions of brute force calculations happening in a matter of seconds
The sheer physical capability required to run all that math is what engineers call compute
Those trillions of calculations are just for your single question
Now multiply that by the millions of people around the world asking their own AI questions at the exact same time
Where does all that math happen?
In a data center. These are giant buildings packed with servers that use chips called GPUs to run many
calculations at once
These data centers are immense covering the scale of several football fields and consuming as much electricity as a small city
To grasp the scale look closely at the aisle on the left
The person walking past the racks gives a sense of proportion for how towering these aisles truly are
The abstract concept of the cloud is actually a sprawling energy-hungry industrial factory for math
A facility of this size means serious external consequences for the people who live nearby
This breakdown illustrates the local impact starting with the electrical grid
Berkeley lab estimates that by 2030 data centers could use about 12% of all U.S. electricity
In some places this added demand is already raising household utility bills
On the top right we see the water footprint
Chips run incredibly hot and cooling a large data center can take roughly a million gallons of water on a hot day
Just to replace what evaporates
Looking at the bottom left
There's the issue of noise
industrial cooling fans have to run 24 hours a day
In certain towns neighbors have sued over the constant hum and lost sleep
Finally on the bottom right we see the reality of permanent jobs
While many people are hired to build a data center far fewer actually work there once the doors open
The heavy infrastructural burdens of our digital convenience are disproportionately carried by the physical towns that host these centers
AI companies are actively trying to adapt
They're securing more electricity designing cooling systems that reuse water and building newer chips that do the same work with less power
But despite these efficiencies the massive and growing scale of AI means it will always require a vast physical footprint
Behind the answer on your screen is a data center
What feels like an isolated weightless interaction to you is a permanent heavy industrial presence in someone else's neighborhood
